title: VPC & On-Prem Radar — Weekly ops brief (Apr 12, 2028)
content:
Context: weekly cross-functional sync for private deployments (VPC + on-prem install teams). This brief captures highlights from the Apr 12 run, decisions, and specific customer blockers that need escalation. Ran 40 minutes; attendees: Maya, Jordan, Liam, Sofia, Arjun, plus field lead for NovaHealth (Elena).

High-level summary:
- Stable cadence on new installs but increased tail latency on a subset of VPC customers when KV cache warmups coincide with node maintenance windows.
- Two active customer incidents this week (NovaHealth and Greenline Retail). Both are at least partially network-related; neither is caused by model runtime bugs.
- Temporary mitigation (traffic shaping + reduced batching) reduced error spikes for NovaHealth but increased token cost; not sustainable.

Incident: NovaHealth (Customer: NovaHealth, Deploy type: VPC — us-east-2)
- Symptom: intermittent 500s and request timeouts during short bursts (observed 04/10–04/12 UTC). Errors cluster around 1–2 minute mark after node recycling.
- Investigation notes:
  - Observed large KV cache misses immediately after rolling maintenance. Prefix cache rehydration is slower than expected for sequences >4096 tokens.
  - Network path traces show increased retry counts on egress to customer firewall during rolling updates — packet drops at ~0.3% rate correlated with retransmits.
  - Kernel-level NIC counters on our side show brief transmit queue saturation when multiple pods reconnect concurrently.
- Temporary mitigations deployed (04/12):
  - Staggered pod restarts with randomized delay (field lead coordination) — decreased simultaneous cache invalidations.
  - Applied traffic shaping rule at Ingress LB for NovaHealth: limit per-connection concurrent streams from 20 -> 6.
- Tradeoffs: reduced error rate but saw 8–12% increase in token latency and ~5% higher token cost.
- Next steps: pursue long-term fix (action items below).

Incident: Greenline Retail (Customer: Greenline, Deploy type: On-prem appliance v1.4)
- Symptom: Embedded inference process sometimes OOMs after prolonged QPS spikes; logs show ephemeral GC pressure and swap thrashing.
- Investigation notes:
  - Instance uses mixed-container cgroup configuration; observed that kernel oom_adj isn't reliably applied to inference container after update script runs.
  - On-prem environment uses older firmware for NICs; observed driver resets coinciding with container restarts.
- Hard stop mitigation: restart helper process on cron when memory > 78% (rolled 04/13). Also requested customer firmware upgrade (ticket open).
- Risk: if customer delays firmware patch, risk of repeat under peak load.

Operational work / changes this week:
- Runbook updates:
  - Added a short diagnostic routine to measure KV cache rehydrate time post-pod-restart (scripts stored in CON-6428). Requires SRE signoff to include in the standard maintenance checklist.
  - New troubleshooting checklist items for on-prem appliances with older NIC firmware (steps to capture ethtool logs and driver reset markers).
- Telemetry improvements:
  - Instrumented per-customer egress retransmit metric (new metric name: private_deploy.egress_retransmits_per_min). Dashboard reference in CON-6428.
  - Added a short latency histogram for first-100-tokens post-warmup to help detect slow rehydrates.
- Deployment cadence:
  - Backfill patch candidate for staggered restart logic to be included in next patch release (target 2028-04-28). Patch will add exponential backoff jitter to pod restarts.

Decisions taken:
- Do not roll global change to batching defaults; instead we'll implement per-customer policy overrides when network path conditions are degraded. Rationale: global change is too disruptive to cost-per-token.
- Escalate NovaHealth case to account team with rollback-eligible window if firmware upgrades needed on their edge devices.

Action items (owner — due):
- (Maya) Draft RFC for "staggered restart with jitter" and post to Confluence. Include performance model and cost tradeoffs — due 2028-04-18. (linked: CON-6428)
- (Jordan) Create a short SRE runbook PR adding KV rehydrate checks to the maintenance window checklist; include exact ethtool commands and expected counters — due 2028-04-15. (GITHUB PR 89)
- (Liam) Build a small load test that simulates concurrent pod reconnects to reproduce transmit queue saturation; share findings with infra team — due 2028-04-20. (JIRA:PD-2112)
- (Sofia) Open formal request with NovaHealth to schedule a controlled maintenance window for firmware verification and to run a staged restart plan — outreach by 2028-04-14.
- (Arjun) Draft an embeddable helper script for on-prem appliances that monitors memory and auto-captures diagnostic tarball on thresholds; get signoff from solutions-eng — due 2028-04-19.

Risks & unresolved questions:
- If multiple customers are on the same maintenance cadence (e.g., weekly kernel updates), we will still get correlated reconnects despite jitter; need a higher-level orchestration approach to globally detect correlated maintenance waves.
- Cost vs. reliability tradeoff: reducing batching helps reliability at the expense of per-token cost. Need product guidance on acceptable band for enterprise SLAs.

Notes to field engineers (short):
- When performing node restarts for customers with long-context workloads (>4k tokens), please flag to ops channel and request a 15-minute stagger window.
- If you hit retransmit spikes, collect tcpdump for 60s, record NIC stats via ethtool -S, and upload to Jira ticket.

Next meeting:
- Weekly sync: Apr 19, 2028 — 09:30 PT. Focus: NovaHealth mitigation progress, load test results, and runbook sign-offs.

Appendix (quick links and logs):
- NovaHealth incident trace (short): JIRA:PD-2104
- Runbook draft: CON-6428
- Infra load repro ticket: JIRA:PD-2112
- PR with runbook changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-playbooks/pull/89
